newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana leader cancels OAU summit trip over S.Leone.
newsitem.headline: Ghana leader cancels OAU summit trip over S.Leone.

text.p: Ghana's President Jerry Rawlings has cancelled his trip to next week's Organisation of African Unity summit following a military coup in Sierra Leone, a cabinet minister said on Friday.

Acting Foreign Minister Kwamena Ahwoi told parliament that Rawlings was in telephone contact with Freetown's new military leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah, trying to persuade him to negotiate a political settlement.

Ahwoi said Rawlings would send a representative to the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit, which opens in Harare on Monday. He said contacts between Rawlings and Koromah, who seized power last Sunday, were at a very delicate stage.
Nigeria has sent troop reinforcements to Freetown and is expected to intervene to restore the former civilian president as soon as an evacuation of foreigners is complete.
Ghana has troops in the Nigerian-led ECOMOG regional intervention force sent to Liberia in 1990.

"Rawlings has already been in contact with his counterparts in the sub-region on the situation, based on an appeal from the central organ of the OAU mechanism for conflict prevention, management and resolution," Ahwoi said.
